correctness.rationale: Checked the dimension-independent two-region norm inequalities directly. Set q=p1+p2, with p2(x+a)=p2(x) from a·Lambda2 subset Z. Because S1 and S1+a⊂S2 are disjoint, ||q(·+a)-q||^2_{S1}<=2||q||^2_{S1∪S2}; the A1 Riesz bound and phase gap m yield ||c1||^2<=2||q||^2/(A1 m^2). On S2, ||p2||^2<=2||q||^2+2 C12||c1||^2 and A2 lower Riesz yields the displayed coefficient reciprocal L. Cauchy-Schwarz with energies (B1+C12)||c1||^2 and <=2 B2||c2||^2 gives U=B1+C12+2B2. Completeness is not inferred from boundedness: translate f1 to S1+a and apply Lambda2 completeness; the remaining Lambda1 Fourier factors (1-e^{-2pi i a·lambda}) are nonzero, so f1=f2=0. The phase gap is positive due to dist(Lambda1,Gamma_a)>0. This reconstructs a full Riesz basis, not just finite-coefficient bounds.
